posts.text:
Wine gets made almost everywhere it can be made — and that turns out to be two narrow ribbons of the planet. One map, and the climate does most of the explaining.

Data: Our World in Data (CC BY)

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ Wine grapes grow mostly between the 30th and 50th parallels, north and south, usually in Mediterranean climates. Shade in those two bands and you have drawn most of this map before looking at a single country.

2/ Three countries make roughly half the world's wine: Italy, France and Spain. Which leads depends on the weather. Italy was ahead in 2021 and 2022; France took the top spot in 2023, the year shown here.

3/ The second tier is where wine stops being European. In 2021, nine countries each made over a million tonnes — and six of them were outside Europe: the US, China, Australia, Chile, Argentina and South Africa.
4/ China is the one people miss. It has been a top-five producer by volume, built in a few decades with imported French technique, and it barely appears in how anyone talks about wine.

5/ The grey carries as much information as the colour. Much of the Middle East is blank. Iran produced wine until 1979 — the vineyards are still there, the fruit now goes to raisins and juice instead.

6/ At the other end of the scale: the UK reported about 354 tonnes in 2021. France makes that much in under an hour. English vineyards are real and growing fast, and on this scale they are still a rounding error.

7/ The top 15 producers account for over 90% of world output. Wine looks global and is in fact intensely concentrated — a short list of countries inside two thin ribbons of latitude.

Data: Our World in Data (CC BY)
